the-rivals-of-amziah-king-cocktail-party.reason: A gimmick premise about bee theft does not carry a 130-minute film, and McConaughey's charm cannot fix the thin setup. The cocktail-party format at Alamo Drafthouse invites distraction, which this script cannot afford.

teenage-sex-and-death-at-camp-miasma-w-l.reason: A clever meta-slasher with real ambition, but the runtime tests patience and the live intro gimmick works only if you're in the right mood. The Alamo Drafthouse screening is built for a crowd, which helps, but this plays better as a late-night event than a solo evening out.

tt0119698.reason: Miyazaki's masterpiece demands the theatrical scale it was made for, and this NYC run is a rare chance to see it projected as intended. The hand-painted animation and compositional depth dissolve into nothing on a small screen.

tt5822536.reason: The third film sustains the warmth and visual invention that made the first two essential family cinema. Dougal Wilson keeps the Peru setting alive with color and genuine charm without sacrificing the humor that works for adults in the theater.

tt0090756.reason: Lynch's masterpiece of American noir perversion demands the big screen and the dark theater it requires. The sound design alone—those industrial drones, that pop song, Penderecki's strings—creates an atmosphere no home setup can match.

tt0040636.reason: A procedural masterpiece that invented the template for every cop show that followed—see it on 35mm at Film Forum before it vanishes. Dassin shot the entire film on real New York streets in 1948, and the restoration lets you feel the pavement under your feet.

tt10954718.reason: Skip the theaters if you have young kids at home—the 89 minutes work fine on a smaller screen without the ticket markup. Peter Hastings adapts DaV Pilkey's comic series with standard animated competence, but nothing here demands a theatrical rescue from a streaming couch.

tt7510222.reason: Skip it; the franchise has run out of ideas and this entry is just a 94-minute toy commercial. The theatrical experience adds nothing that wouldn't be better on a home screen in a few months.

tt29612071.reason: Skip it; the premise collapses under its own randomness, and there's nothing in the execution or venue to justify the trip. A 95-minute animated comedy about alien abduction and cat villainy has no theatrical value that wouldn't play better at home.

tt0087182.reason: Lynch's version is a singular, visionary failure that rewards curiosity about how a master director approaches unfilmable source material. The grotesque production design and warped narrative logic make this essential viewing for anyone serious about science fiction cinema, regardless of its reputation.

tt0066492.reason: Skip it; this 1970 creature feature is a clumsy exploitation film that wastes a capable director on a thin premise and lazy execution. Freddie Francis deserved better material than B-movie dreck about a caveman in a cage.

tt38645461.reason: Skip it unless you're in the mood for a light competition doc that plays like a sports movie about cheese. The premise is charming but the theatrical experience doesn't offer much that streaming won't deliver just as well from your couch.

tt38084416.reason: A 4D gimmick applied to a film that works because of its restraint and imagination, not sensory bombardment. The 75-minute runtime suggests heavy cuts to a masterpiece that demands its full form.

tt37091259.reason: A modest indie comedy about grief that works best if you connect with Bruce Campbell's understated direction and the intimate pacing of a 90-minute road movie. The Alamo Drafthouse venues are solid but not a draw—this film has no theatrical urgency and plays just fine at home later.
